opening_message:
Ticket 1: John Rodriguez (employee ID E049) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E049.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: John Rodriguez (E049), Analyst, full-time employee. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access (admin requires owning role, which does not apply here). Grant write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E049 (John Rodriguez) is a contractor with basic security training (note in shared memory said full-time; security record takes precedence). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training => maximum is read. Requested write exceeds maximum, so grant read.
reason: There is a conflict between the HR note (full-time) and the Security note (contractor). The Security agent checked E049's employment type and security training in the security database, which is authoritative for access, and reports contractor with basic training. Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; basic training means the maximum is read. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
